title: Two-party Safe
summary: Two owners configure a Safe so both signatures are required for every transaction.

receipts.claim: This tag contains the reviewed Safe 1.4.1 implementation.
receipts.boundary: Source identity alone does not identify a Safe proxy or its configuration.

receipts.claim: Safe's registry maps the released 1.4.1 singleton to this canonical address and code hash.
receipts.boundary: The singleton deployment is not the party-specific proxy instance.

receipts.claim: Safe defines owners, threshold, transaction hashes, nonces, and signatures.
receipts.boundary: Documentation does not establish the economic suitability of 2-of-2 control.

gaps: No delivery, refund, or adjudication condition

title: Linear payment stream
summary: A sender deposits tokens that become withdrawable by a recipient continuously over time.

receipts.claim: The public repository contains Sablier's Solana Lockup program source.
receipts.boundary: The repository main branch may move after a deployed release.

receipts.claim: Sablier publishes this address as the official Lockup deployment.
receipts.boundary: The published address does not by itself prove current source-to-program identity.

receipts.claim: Sablier lists a Cantina review for SolSab.
receipts.boundary: An audit is scoped to its reviewed revision and is not a guarantee.

gaps: No selected token mint or funded stream

title: Vesting wallet
summary: A beneficiary receives native or ERC-20 assets according to a linear schedule.

receipts.claim: OpenZeppelin publishes the VestingWallet implementation in Contracts 5.x.
receipts.boundary: The moving master branch is not a pinned deployment artifact.

receipts.claim: The API documents linear vesting behavior and release functions.
receipts.boundary: The primitive must be deployed, configured, funded, and reviewed in its application.

gaps: No beneficiary, schedule, asset, funding, or deployment receipt

title: Expiring token permission
summary: A token owner gives a spender an amount- and time-bounded ERC-20 permission using Permit2.

receipts.claim: Uniswap publishes Permit2's AllowanceTransfer and SignatureTransfer implementation.
receipts.boundary: Repository source does not identify the user's token approval or signed permit.

receipts.claim: Uniswap deployment records identify the canonical Permit2 address.
receipts.boundary: One chain record does not prove availability or code identity on every named chain.

receipts.claim: Permit2 supports signature-based approvals, bounded allowances, transfers, and revocation.
receipts.boundary: The integrating spender contract and token behavior remain separate dependencies.

gaps: No review of the integrating spender
